manual_findings.source: Registered Git remote URL or repository-controlled local origin URL
manual_findings.sink: Automatic GitHub-token lookup and go-git BasicAuth on remote branch discovery
manual_findings.trust_boundary: User/repository-selected URL versus stored owner GitHub credential

manual_findings.review: Shared IsGitHubTokenRemote requires HTTPS, exact github.com hostname, default/443 port and no URL userinfo. Both route branches use it before looking up a token; ListRemoteBranches rejects unsafe token-bearing destinations before transport creation. Existing go-git v5.19.3 strips credentials on cross-origin redirects. Broader source transport/SSRF policy remains open.
manual_findings.regression_check_status: TestGitHubTokenOriginBoundary covers authority confusion and an HTTP request sentinel; TestRepoBranchesOnlySelectGitHubCredentialsForTrustedHTTPSOrigin exercises encrypted-secret selection for both registered Git remotes and local checkout origins.

Tests cover valid files, safe symlinks, outside paths, file/directory symlink escapes, missing files, and uninitialized stores. manual_findings.source: First-run/reloaded JWT signing and encryption key files

manual_findings.trust_boundary: Persistent credential/session identity across concurrent processes, file read failures, and process restart

manual_findings.review: Shared os.Root-based temporary write/sync/close and no-overwrite Link publication preserve existing entries and load the winning key. Existing unreadable/malformed keys fail without replacement. API/scan/fix worker startup fails before backend/database initialization on invalid keys. Encryption-key snapshots are atomically published and copied. Existing raw JWT/hex encryption formats and environment precedence are unchanged. Rotation/versioned decryption, distributed filesystem and crash/power-loss qualification remain open.

manual_findings.source: Persisted prepared-workspace path and administrative TTL request

manual_findings.trust_boundary: Temporary-source ownership and cooperating process lifetime versus filesystem deletion
manual_findings.disposition: Scoped cleanup/lifetime implementation repaired; independent review and distributed/orphan-job qualification pending
manual_findings.review: Shared native regular-file leases protect Git/SSH preparation, resumed/local reuse, CLI scanning and existing deferred enrichment cleanup. Exclusive nonblocking lease acquisition precedes os.Root-confined direct-child deletion. Stable namespace guards protect lease creation/pruning without serializing recursive deletion. Strict bounded TTL parsing rejects invalid/overflowing requests; API/UI report in-use retention and real failures. Default temporary metadata is per-user; configured service roots require a common configuration and filesystem identity. Does not qualify independently surviving Docker/Kubernetes jobs, noncooperating old workers or RWX mounts.

manual_findings.exploitability: Confirmed two-file versus one-file and symlink versus regular-file serialization collisions without a SHA-256 collision; executable mode changes were invisible. All three fail on the old implementation.
manual_findings.disposition: Versioned framing implementation repaired; atomic source snapshots and independent review remain open
manual_findings.review: Sorted v2 entries have length-framed path/payload, type and permissions; directory entries included, .git pointers/directories excluded, symlink text not target read, special files rejected, opened regular-file identity checked and detected in-read mutations fail. Legacy digest recovery fails safely rather than assuming compatible identity. Not an atomic filesystem snapshot or complete resource-limit guarantee.
